title: Resume & LinkedIn Toolkit
subtitle: How to Build a Career Brand That Gets Noticed and Shortlisted

sections.title: Why Resumes and LinkedIn Are Your Career Brand

blocks.text: Your resume and LinkedIn are not documents—they’re your **career storefront.** Before recruiters speak with you, they look at these two things. A polished resume gets you interviews; a strong LinkedIn gets you discovered.
Think of it as inbound vs outbound marketing:

blocks.label: Reflection
blocks.text: Which one is currently stronger for you—resume or LinkedIn?

sections.title: Resume Basics: Structure & Format That Work Globally

blocks.text: Recruiters often spend **only seconds** on a first resume scan. Keep it clean:

items: Length: 1 page (US, UK), 2 pages (Europe, India for >8 years exp).
Sections: Summary, Experience, Education, Skills, Certifications.
Don’t include photos, DOB, marital status (except where required like Germany).

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Audit your resume for formatting errors. Note the three biggest fixes.
Your summary = your elevator pitch. It must:

items: “Strategy consultant with 7 years’ experience across two global consulting firms, specializing in digital transformation and market entry. MBA from Warwick. Seeking leadership roles in consulting or corporate strategy.”

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Write a 3-sentence professional summary.
The difference between a weak resume and a strong one is **impact.**

rows: “Developed client presentations on digital strategy, influencing a $25M implementation.”

blocks.text: Formula = Action Verb + Task + Impact + Number.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Rewrite 1 bullet from your resume with measurable results.

items: **Tech:** Showcase product ownership, data-driven decisions, coding/project tools.

sections.title: LinkedIn Basics: Headline, Summary, and Experience

blocks.text: Your LinkedIn headline is SEO gold.

rows: “Strategy Consultant | Digital Transformation | Ex-Deloitte | MBA Warwick.”

blocks.text: Your summary should be future-facing.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Write one headline that positions you for your dream role.

sections.title: Optimizing LinkedIn for Recruiter Search (Keywords + SEO)

blocks.text: LinkedIn works like Google. Recruiters search with keywords: “Data Analyst SQL Python.” If those words aren’t in your profile, you won’t show up.
Tips:

items: Use keywords in headline, summary, skills.
Add the skills that matter for your target role (LinkedIn allows up to 100).

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Search a dream job description. Extract 5 keywords and add them to your LinkedIn profile.
Recommendations = credibility. Get them from managers, clients, colleagues.

items: “Priya rebuilt our reporting process in three months and made every client review easier to run. She is the analyst I’d hire again first.”

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Ask 1 ex-colleague for a LinkedIn recommendation today.
